qa.scope: Final QA of happy-dev incident-repair fix set, including iteration-3 fail-closed live-daemon compatibility protection. Verification used static inspection and non-destructive checks only.
qa.user_verbatim_complaint: Fix Happy recovery/session tracking debt and targeted OOM protection, excluding coarse whole-daemon memory limits; add live-daemon compatibility protection so recovery cannot call an old daemon /spawn-session that ignores resumeSessionId.
qa.overall_assessment: PASS. Recovery now restores only through daemon /spawn-session, keeps external_restored=0, respects tombstones, prevents stable low-count snapshot pollution, and fails closed before spawning when the live daemon cannot prove resume-aware /spawn-session support. OOM guard targets session cgroups/process groups and no whole-daemon memory cap or Codex removal was found.

build_verification.skip_reason: User explicitly prohibited live stop/restart/reload and restore; this cycle changes operational scripts plus CLI source. QA ran TypeScript noEmit and safe syntax/static checks instead of deploying or restarting daemons.

deployment_prerequisites_before_live_use: Build/install the compatible happy-cli artifact for every daemon home that should support recovery. The recovery script is already installed, but current live daemon processes may predate resume-aware /spawn-session support.

Restart affected daemons only through the sanctioned safe-daemon-restart SOP (for dev: /root/bin/safe-daemon-restart.sh dev --reason '<reason>'; production/default/jade/qijie require explicit operator approval and the matching sanctioned SOP). Do not use raw systemctl or kill.
Run systemd daemon-reload (operator-authorized, not done by QA) before relying on the changed happy-memory-emergency-guard.service OOMScoreAdjust/Nice/IO settings.

After authorized restart/reload, re-run only non-destructive proof checks first: bash -n scripts, systemd-analyze verify, daemon_resume_spawn_support_proof for each daemon pid, and a /list schema/mapping check. Only then consider an operator-approved restore.
Do not run recovery restore against live sessions until the preflight proof passes for the relevant daemon; current behavior correctly fails closed when proof cannot be established.
